title: Introduce Query-Context Consistency Gate and CI signal broker
author: Marisol Chen
release_notes: Add a CI gate that enforces context-consistency for multi-turn queries with hysteresis smoothing and a CI-side signal broker; exposes Prometheus metrics and a lightweight reporter to the existing eval pipeline.
description: Motivation: Flapping regressions observed in multi-turn prompt sets where small context shuffles or appended system notes produced outsized score deltas. This change introduces a Query-Context Consistency Gate (QCC Gate) plus a CI signal broker that aggregates multiple eval signals (semantic fidelity, paraphrase invariance, turnwise coherence) and applies temporal hysteresis to avoid noisy failures. Scope: gate implemented as an opt-in CI hook for eval-harness that can be attached to the GitHub CI pipeline; includes a broker service used only during CI to normalize and fuse signals, a lightweight smoothing policy with configurable window and thresholds, Prometheus-compatible metrics, unit and integration tests, and documentation for usage. Checklist: [x] implement core gate logic and hysteresis policy; [x] add CI broker and REST shim; [x] expose metrics and CI reporter; [x] add smoke and integration tests; [x] update docs and quickstart. Backwards compat: non-default behavior; no runtime behavioral changes unless gate enabled in CI config. How it works: the CI run posts batched eval traces to the broker; the broker computes per-cohort aggregated statistics, applies a rolling-window hysteresis (min-streak, cool-down), and returns a pass/soft-fail/hard-fail assessment. Soft-fail maps to a non-blocking annotation and automated issue template; hard-fail blocks the merge. The gate consumes multiple signal inputs and supports weighting overrides per-prompt-set. Related: ENG-2109 (flapping multi-turn regressions), ENG-2147 (eval signal normalizer).
